findings.title: CloudTrail not logging
findings.description: No active CloudTrail trail covers us-east-1. Without an audit log there is no record of who did what - incident response becomes guesswork.
findings.remediation: Create a multi-region trail: aws cloudtrail create-trail --name org-trail --s3-bucket-name <log-bucket> --is-multi-region-trail && aws cloudtrail start-logging --name org-trail

findings.title: SSH open to the internet
findings.description: Security group 'bastion-ssh' (sg-941739722f78f4e54) allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0. Internet-exposed admin/database ports are constantly brute-forced by automated bots.
findings.remediation: Restrict the source to your office/VPN CIDR, or remove the rule and use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access.

findings.title: RDP open to the internet
findings.description: Security group 'win-jumpbox' (sg-3484e61e3c3fd1b5a) allows RDP (port 3389) from 0.0.0.0/0. Internet-exposed admin/database ports are constantly brute-forced by automated bots.
findings.remediation: Restrict the source to your office/VPN CIDR, or remove the rule and use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access.

findings.title: S3 bucket publicly accessible via ACL
findings.description: Bucket 'acme-customer-exports' has an ACL granting READ to everyone on the internet. Public buckets are one of the most common causes of cloud data breaches.

findings.title: MySQL open to the internet
findings.description: Security group 'legacy-mysql' (sg-04f9754666cc3a8d7) allows MySQL (port 3306) from 0.0.0.0/0. Internet-exposed admin/database ports are constantly brute-forced by automated bots.
findings.remediation: Restrict the source to your office/VPN CIDR, or remove the rule and use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access.

findings.title: Console user without MFA
findings.description: User 'jsmith' can sign in to the AWS console with only a password. A phished or reused password gives an attacker full access.
findings.remediation: Enable a virtual or hardware MFA device for this user and enforce MFA with an IAM policy.

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: Database 'orders-db' has a public endpoint reachable from the internet.

findings.title: S3 Block Public Access disabled
findings.description: Bucket 'acme-customer-exports' does not have all four Block Public Access settings enabled, so a single bad ACL or policy change could expose its data to the internet.

findings.title: EBS encryption-by-default disabled
findings.description: New EBS volumes in us-east-1 are not encrypted automatically, so disk snapshots could leak data if shared or copied.

findings.title: Access key older than 90 days
findings.description: Access key AKIADEMOSTALEKEY0001 for 'ci-deploy-bot' was created 2026-04-15 (214 days ago). Long-lived keys are frequently leaked in code repos and laptops.
findings.remediation: Rotate the key (create new, update apps, deactivate old) or move to IAM roles / SSO.

findings.title: AdministratorAccess attached directly to user
findings.description: User 'jsmith' has full admin rights attached directly. This breaks least privilege and makes access hard to audit.
findings.remediation: Grant permissions through IAM groups or roles scoped to the job, and remove the direct attachment.

findings.title: Weak or missing account password policy
findings.description: The account password policy is missing or allows passwords shorter than 14 characters.

findings.title: RDS storage not encrypted
findings.description: Database 'orders-db' stores data unencrypted at rest.
findings.remediation: Snapshot the DB, copy the snapshot with --kms-key-id, and restore from the encrypted copy.

findings.title: S3 versioning disabled
findings.description: Bucket 'acme-customer-exports' does not keep object versions, so deleted or overwritten (e.g. ransomware-encrypted) objects cannot be recovered.
